## Selected Work

### Project Anveshan — Open Deep Research Operating System
- Category: Agentic AI · Multi-Agent Orchestration
- Badge: Open Source OS
- GitHub: https://github.com/Jeevanpaul766/PROJECT-ANVESHAN

**Problem:** Single-prompt AI search and naive RAG suffer from severe context degradation, citation hallucination, and lack of methodical critique when investigating complex academic questions.

**Solution:** A 5-agent LangGraph Deep Research OS with citation provenance, adversarial critique, novelty-saturation stop detection, and disk checkpointing, guaranteeing 100% verifiable citation integrity across arXiv, CrossRef, and Semantic Scholar.

**What I Built:** Engineered an autonomous multi-agent state machine (Orchestrator, Academic Search Manager, Evidence Extractor, Adversarial Critic, and Synthesizer) with local-first Ollama execution, React + Vite SSE live streaming dashboard, and Python SDK with hierarchical LangSmith tracing.

**Architecture:**
- Context: Researchers need autonomous multi-step investigation that can run for 3 to 60 minutes across academic registries without hallucinating URLs or losing state mid-investigation.
- Role: Lead Architect & Open Source Creator. Designed the complete 5-agent state graph, memory checkpointing engine, Python SDK, and React Vite streaming UI.
- Hard Part: Preventing infinite loops and information redundancy during multi-hop investigation. Engineered a streak-based novelty-saturation engine that computes information gain delta (ΔI) across iterations and triggers convergence when returns diminish.
- Validation: Benchmarked on rigorous multi-domain academic queries; achieved 100% verified DOI/arXiv citation integrity with zero hallucinated links and 3-level hierarchical LangSmith waterfall trace coverage.
- Outcome: Open-source deep research system capable of generating comprehensive, publication-grade dossiers with verifiable academic source trees and full pause/resume checkpointing.

**Metrics:**
- Agent Topology: 5 Coordinated Agents
- Citation Integrity: 100% Grounded (No Hallucinations)
- Registries: arXiv, CrossRef, Semantic Scholar

**Tech Stack:** LangGraph, Multi-Agent, LangSmith, Python SDK, Hybrid RAG, React / Vite, Ollama, SSE Streaming

### NyayaPath — Dual-Regime Legal Guidance Agent
- Category: Legal NLP · Deterministic Guardrails
- Badge: Educational Agent
- GitHub: https://github.com/Jeevanpaul766/NyayaPath

**Problem:** India's transition from colonial statutes (IPC, CrPC) to modern criminal codes (BNS, BNSS) creates severe legal misdirection when generic LLMs confuse identical section numbers with completely different legal meanings (e.g., Section 482).

**Solution:** A 12-node cyclic LangGraph agent with date-of-offence temporal routing, local Hybrid RAG over 2,820 indexed statutory sections (ChromaDB + BM25 + RRF), two-stage asymmetric crisis gates, and pure Python zero-LLM output sanitizers.

**What I Built:** Architected the 12-node cyclic StateGraph in Python 3.11 with FastAPI backend, ChromaDB vector store, BM25 lexical retriever, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, deterministic section allowlist, React 19 Vite TypeScript frontend, and end-to-end LangSmith telemetry.

**Architecture:**
- Context: Educational legal tech system designed to demonstrate how deterministic guardrails and temporal routing resolve constitutional Article 20(1) ex-post-facto statute collisions.
- Role: Sole AI Engineer. Implemented the 12-node cyclic state machine, statutory indexing pipeline, intent classifiers, and print-ready PDF legal memorandum export.
- Hard Part: Resolving Section 482 collision: in CrPC it denotes High Court Quashing powers, whereas in BNSS it denotes Anticipatory Bail. Solved by routing offence dates strictly through temporal classifiers before retrieval.
- Validation: 140 passing unit tests and a 25-case automated evaluation suite spanning 7 legal categories; zero hallucinated sections allowed past the deterministic output sanitizer.
- Outcome: Interactive legal orientation console generating structured 7-part legal memoranda with millisecond telemetry tracking across local Ollama Qwen2.5:7b models.

**Disclaimer:** Portfolio & educational project demonstrating advanced agentic AI architectures and guardrails. Strictly not legal advice and not a legal service.

**Metrics:**
- Statutory Corpus: 2,820 Partitioned Sections
- Graph Complexity: 12-Node Cyclic StateGraph
- Safety Evaluation: 140 Unit Tests Passed

**Tech Stack:** LangGraph (12-Node), ChromaDB, BM25 / RRF, FastAPI, LangSmith, Deterministic Guardrails, React 19 / Vite, Python 3.11+

### WorldTrendz — Production Conversational AI iOS Application
- Category: Production AI · Mobile & Backend
- Badge: Production · App Store
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/worldtrendz/id6761761956

**Problem:** E-commerce mobile shoppers face friction navigating large catalogs and require instant, context-aware conversational shopping assistance with low latency on mobile devices.

**Solution:** A production conversational AI application published live on the Apple App Store, backed by secure asynchronous FastAPI services, robust context management, and multi-model LLM orchestration.

**What I Built:** Engineered the production AI backend microservices in Python and FastAPI, handling live user sessions, stateless JWT authentication, context window pruning, product catalog retrieval, and multi-model failover routing.

**Architecture:**
- Context: Commercial conversational application for WorldTrendz LLC published on the Apple App Store serving real live end-users.
- Role: Freelance AI & Backend Engineer. Responsible for the FastAPI cloud backend, multi-model orchestration, security, and context memory.
- Hard Part: Maintaining low latency and zero session state drops under concurrent mobile traffic while managing token budget constraints across conversation turns.
- Validation: Successfully passed Apple App Store technical review and deployed to live production users with automated health check monitoring.
- Outcome: Live mobile application with active users on iOS, demonstrating end-to-end production backend reliability and conversational AI orchestration.

**Metrics:**
- Deployment: Apple App Store (Live)
- Backend Latency: Sub-second Streaming
- Architecture: Async FastAPI + Multi-LLM

**Tech Stack:** FastAPI, Production GenAI, Apple App Store, Multi-Model LLMs, Context Management, Python, Docker

## Field Notes (Technical Writing)

### Tracing Agent Workflows: Moving Beyond Naive Demos
- Category: Observability & Multi-Agent Systems
- Date: March 2026
- Read Time: 6 min

Why traditional HTTP request/response logging breaks down in non-deterministic multi-agent graphs, and how trace spans, execution state trees, and token consumption metrics keep production agents debuggable.

Key Takeaways:
- Treat agent loops as state machines with discrete, immutable transitions rather than monolithic chains.
- Track tool call latency and output schema conformance at each branch to isolate regressions early.
- Implement deterministic calculation verification when generative outputs involve quantitative reasoning.

### Designing Resilient RAG: Lessons from Hybrid Dense-Sparse Retrieval
- Category: Information Retrieval & NLP
- Date: February 2026
- Read Time: 8 min

Pure vector cosine similarity routinely fails on exact alphanumeric statutory codes, product IDs, and domain acronyms. How combining Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with cross-encoder rerankers eliminates retrieval blind spots.

Key Takeaways:
- Combine BM25 for keyword/code exactness with dense embeddings for semantic nuance.
- Use cross-encoder reranking on top 25 candidates to filter out false-positive embedding clusters.
- Establish strict citation grounding: reject generated answers when retrieved context lacks affirmative support.

### Running Small Language Models on Local Silicon: Practical Constraints
- Category: Local Inference & Edge AI
- Date: January 2026
- Read Time: 7 min

A deep dive into GGUF quantization levels, KV cache memory footprint, and prompt formatting quirks when running Llama 3 / Mistral 8B models locally for private automated workflows.

Key Takeaways:
- 4-bit quantization (Q4_K_M) retains ~98% of extraction capability while halving memory footprint.
- Context compression and iterative chunk summarization outperform throwing 32k tokens into a single prompt.
- Zero cloud egress makes local SLMs the premier choice for proprietary internal document synthesis.
